<explanation>
To produce a clear, accurate system design diagram for the MediaPipe repository, follow these steps:

1. Identify the project’s type and purpose  
   • This is an open-source on-device machine‐learning pipeline framework.  
   • It provides:  
     – A core C++ Graph execution engine (calculators, packets, streams).  
     – Prebuilt “Solutions” (Vision, Audio, Text tasks).  
     – Platform bindings (Python, Java/Android, Objective-C/iOS, Web/JavaScript).  
     – Model Maker tooling (Python) to customize models.  
     – Examples and demos across desktop, mobile, web.  
     – A unified build & packaging setup (Bazel, Docker).

2. Decompose the file tree into top‐level components  
   • Build & Deployment: WORKSPACE, BUILD.bazel, .bazelrc, Dockerfiles, CI workflows.  
   • Core Framework: mediapipe/framework (Graph, Calculator, Packet, Executor, Scheduler).  
   • Calculators & Formats: mediapipe/calculators/, mediapipe/formats/, mediapipe/gpu utilities.  
   • Graph Definitions: mediapipe/graphs/ (preconfigured pipelines in .pbtxt).  
   • Modules: mediapipe/modules/ (reusable subgraphs with .proto and .pbtxt).  
   • Tasks & Solutions APIs: mediapipe/tasks/ (C/C++, Python, Java, Web wrappers).  
   • Model Maker: mediapipe/model_maker/ (Python code for data pipelines and training).  
   • Examples: mediapipe/examples/ (Android, iOS, desktop, Coral)  
   • Bindings: mediapipe/python/, mediapipe/java/, mediapipe/objc/, mediapipe/web/.  
   • Utilities & Third-party: mediapipe/util/, third_party/ (FlatBuffers, TensorFlow, XNNPack).

3. Draw main components and their relationships  
   a. Core Components  
     – Graph Execution Engine (C++): builds & runs directed pipelines of calculators.  
     – Calculators: modular units processing Packets (image, tensor, audio, detection).  
     – Packet & Stream Abstractions: typed data containers flowing between calculators.  
     – Scheduler & Executors: manage threading, GPU/WebGPU contexts.  
   b. API & Bindings Layers  
     – C API (mediapipe/tasks/c): thin wrapper around core for Task components.  
     – C++ Task Library (mediapipe/tasks/cc): composable graphs for Vision/Text/Audio.  
     – Python Bindings: pybind11 wrappers for Graph and Packets, plus high-level Tasks (mediapipe/python, mediapipe/tasks/python).  
     – Java/Android: JNI layer and Android components exposing Graph & Tasks.  
     – Objective-C/iOS: Obj-C wrappers around C++ Graph & tasks.  
     – Web/JavaScript: WebAssembly modules with WASM fileset, JavaScript APIs.  
   c. Solutions & Models  
     – Prebuilt Models: TFLite, TensorFlow SavedModels in mediapipe/models and mediapipe/tasks/testdata.  
     – MediaPipe Tasks: high-level classes orchestrating Graph configs plus model loading.  
     – Model Maker: pipelines for training and exporting custom models.  
   d. Examples & Demos  
     – Platform examples instantiate GraphRunner/TaskRunner with sample Graph configs and renderers.  
     – Coral examples interface with EdgeTPU delegates.  
   e. Build & Packaging  
     – Bazel orchestrates builds for all languages and platforms.  
     – Dockerfiles create reproducible Linux and manylinux containerized builds.  
     – shell scripts for Android/iOS setup, opencv, LLM inference.  

4. Highlight architectural patterns  
   • Pipeline Pattern: Graph of calculators connected by streams.  
   • Plugin/Registry: calculators registered via macros and discovered at runtime.  
   • Adapter/Bridge: per-platform bindings (C++ → Python, Java, Objective-C, JS).  
   • Builder: API2/3 graph builder fluent interfaces.  
   • Factory: TaskRunner factories for different running modes (live, sync, async).  

5. Technologies & Frameworks  
   • C++, Bazel, Docker, FlatBuffers, Protocol Buffers, pybind11.  
   • TensorFlow Lite, TensorFlow, XNNPACK, WebGPU, OpenGL, Metal.  
   • Kotlin/Java (Android), Swift/Obj-C (iOS), TypeScript/JavaScript (Web).  
   • Python (Tasks, Model Maker, Examples).  

6. Tailor diagram to a full-stack on-device ML framework  
   • Layer 1: Build & CI (Bazel, Docker)  
   • Layer 2: Core Engine (Graph, Scheduler, Executors)  
   • Layer 3: Calculators & Formats (audio, video, image, tensor)  
   • Layer 4: Predefined Graphs & Modules (pbtxt, proto)  
   • Layer 5: Task APIs & Model Management (C/C++, Python, Java, iOS, Web)  
   • Layer 6: Platform SDKs & Examples (Android apps, iOS apps, Web demos, Python scripts)  
   • Layer 7: Model Maker & Data Pipelines  

7. Diagramming guidelines  
   • Draw each major component as a labeled box.  
   • Use directional arrows to indicate data flow:  
     – Input sources (camera, mic) → GraphRunner → Calculators → Outputs (render, callback).  
     – Model loading & delegates flow into inference calculators.  
   • Color-code by layer:  
     – Core (e.g., blue), API bindings (green), Tasks (orange), Examples (gray), Build (purple).  
   • Shape variants:  
     – Cylinders for data stores/models, parallelograms for scripts/tools, rectangles for modules.  
   • Annotate key protocols: gRPC/IPC not used here; internal APIs via Protobufs.  

8. Level of detail  
   • Capture all architectural elements (engine, modules, tasks, bindings).  
   • Avoid every single folder; focus on logical groupings.  
   • Ensure clarity: show how data enters, moves through calculators, and exits.  

By following these steps and layering components from the build system through core engine, modules, APIs, and examples, you’ll create a detailed, platform-agnostic system design diagram that accurately represents the MediaPipe architecture.  
</explanation>
